description:
Two parsers answer "what integer does this text name" in lib, and two answer "what float". The String versions are wrong where the Integer and Float versions are right.

Measured on `run`, near develop a6ae5759d:
- String.to_integer("-9223372036854775808") raises ArithmeticError. Elixir, and Integer.parse("-9223372036854775808"), give {-9223372036854775808, ""}.
- String.to_float("99999999999999999999.5") raises ArithmeticError. Float.parse gives {1.0e20, ""}.

Cause:
- String.to_integer (lib/string.fz:1076) builds the positive magnitude with acc * 10 + d and negates it at the end, so i64's minimum overflows on the way. Integer.parse (lib/integer.fz:62-71) accumulates below zero for exactly this reason; its comment says so.
- String.to_float (lib/string.fz:1129-1138, float_magnitude) builds whole and fraction parts as integers through the same digits_value. A whole part past 64 bits overflows, and whole + fraction / 10^n is not correctly rounded. Float.parse is the correctly rounding authority (lib/json.fz relies on it for that).

Fix: one implementation per question. String.to_integer(s) is Integer.parse(s) when the whole text is consumed and raises ArgumentError otherwise, as in Elixir. String.to_float is the same with Float.parse. digits_value, digits_fold, float_of, float_magnitude and pow10 in lib/string.fz are deleted once nothing else calls them; check their other callers first.

Acceptance: a fixture on all three paths covering i64 min and max, "-0", "+5", an empty string, "12x" (raises ArgumentError), a 20-digit whole part to String.to_float, and a value whose naive whole + fraction / 10^n rounds differently from Float.parse (find one; if none exists in range, say so). Red first.

Related: the JSON rewrite that converts integers from their text, as floats already are (pending the user's decision), would call String.to_integer, so this lands first.
Probe files: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/ebbfffd8-2561-4da7-bcda-f9a316d00a1e/scratchpad/ovf/ (q.fz, s.fz).

comments.text: Folds fz-sc8.59 (closed as duplicate): String.to_float must also parse exponents ("1.0e3" -> 1000.0) and raise ArgumentError where Elixir does; delegating to Float.parse covers it. Collision: fz-nhb.17 (String.index_of/2, lib/string.fz 680/742/775) and fz-nhb.12 (lib/*.fz specs) edit lib/string.fz; second to land rebases.

title: String.to_integer and String.to_float convert through Integer.parse and Float.parse
